question: Which of these is a classic example of a positive feedback loop in the human body?

options.A: Parathyroid hormone halting when blood calcium levels normalize
options.B: Insulin stopping the release of glucose once blood sugar drops
options.C: Oxytocin release intensifying uterine contractions during childbirth
options.D: Thyroid hormone stopping pituitary TSH release when levels are high

explanation: Unlike negative feedback, positive feedback amplifies a signal! During labor, oxytocin makes contractions stronger, which releases even *more* oxytocin until the baby is born. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T5#GNS211_U1_T5_h8)

question: A kitchen worker comes in with a sudden case of watery diarrhea and a mild fever. What should be done immediately?

options.A: Ask them to wash dishes with hot water instead
options.B: Take them off food handling duties right away
options.C: Tell them to swallow an anti-diarrhea drug and keep working
options.D: Let them work as long as they wear two pairs of gloves

explanation: Any worker showing signs of a tummy bug must be kept away from food immediately to stop germs from spreading to everyone else. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h4)

question: Expired medications and leftover vaccines belong to which waste category?

options.A: Radioactive waste
options.B: Pharmaceutical waste
options.C: Pathological waste
options.D: General domestic waste

explanation: You got it! Drugs and medicines always fall under pharmaceutical waste guidelines. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h5)

question: A parent is cooking soup with a toddler playing nearby. Which simple kitchen habit prevents scalds?

options.A: Turning the pot handle inward toward the back of the stove
options.B: Leaving the pot lid slightly open so steam can escape quickly
options.C: Keeping a dry dish towel draped over the front stove knobs
options.D: Placing the pot on the front right burner for easier viewing

explanation: Exactly! Turning handles toward the back stops curious little hands from grabbing them and pulling hot food down. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h2)

question: Why do new mothers need close nursing watch right after delivery?

options.A: Because the mother is at high risk for hemorrhage and infection
options.B: Because the newborn baby requires constant intravenous fluids
options.C: Because mothers cannot produce milk during the first week
options.D: Because routine vital signs are no longer necessary after birth

explanation: The body goes through massive changes right after birth, making those early hours prime time for bleeding and infections. Vigilance saves lives! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h6)

question: How do educators officially define true "learning"?

options.A: A permanent change in behavior or knowledge from experience
options.B: Attending all scheduled classroom lectures and clinicals
options.C: Memorizing facts for a nursing board examination
options.D: The physical growth of the brain during young adulthood

explanation: Learning isn't just about growing older or cramming for a test—it's when your actual knowledge or actions shift because of real experiences. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U8_T1#GST321_U8_T1_h1)

question: In global polio campaigns, what does the abbreviation 'AFP' stand for?

options.A: Asymmetrical Facial Palsy
options.B: Active Fever Protocol
options.C: Advanced Functional Pathology
options.D: Acute Flaccid Paralysis

explanation: You're doing great! AFP stands for acute flaccid paralysis—the key sign health workers watch out for to catch hidden polio cases early. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T15#GNS313_U2_T15_h6)

question: Which of these is a biophysiological measure?

options.A: Interview transcript text
options.B: Open-ended survey response
options.C: Blood glucose level
options.D: Patient satisfaction score

explanation: Biophysiological measures are physical or chemical checks on the body, like checking blood sugar or temperature. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T15#GNS217_U3_T15_h3)

question: A patient is getting intravenous Amphotericin B for a severe kidney fungal infection. Which lab tests should you check most closely?

options.A: Platelet count and bleeding time
options.B: Liver enzymes and bilirubin levels
options.C: Serum sodium and potassium levels
options.D: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen

explanation: Because Amphotericin B is harsh on the kidneys, we always monitor kidney function markers like creatinine and BUN closely. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T3#GNS223_U8_T3_h3)

question: What does 'therapeutic use of self' mean in nursing?

options.A: Using your personality and insights to connect with patients
options.B: Hiding all personal feelings behind a cold professional mask
options.C: Acting as a close personal friend outside of work hours
options.D: Sharing your own personal medical history with every patient

explanation: Spot on! It means using your own communication style and warmth on purpose to build trust and help the patient feel safe. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h2)

question: What is 'primary non-fulfillment' when talking about medication adherence?

options.A: The patient forgets to take afternoon doses only
options.B: The patient stops taking drugs after feeling better
options.C: The patient never fills or picks up the new prescription
options.D: The patient cuts their pills in half to save money

explanation: Think of it as step one: they leave the clinic with a script, but never actually buy or pick up the medicine. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T3#GNS215_U4_T3_h2)

question: Why is it important to move mental health care beyond hospital walls into communities?

options.A: Because doctors prefer working outdoors with crowds
options.B: Because hospitals are too expensive to clean
options.C: Because community members can replace trained psychiatrists entirely
options.D: Because daily social roots and support systems heavily influence well-being

explanation: Mental health is deeply connected to a person's everyday environment, making local community support essential for lasting recovery and prevention. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's serum albumin lab result before giving a protein-bound drug?

options.A: To measure the exact body fat percentage
options.B: To see how well the kidneys are making urine
options.C: To determine if there is a bacterial infection
options.D: To check if the patient is at risk for drug toxicity

explanation: Low albumin levels change the balance of bound vs. free drug. Checking this lab value helps you keep the patient safe from unexpected high doses of active medicine. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h8)

question: Why is establishing trust early so important for a home health nurse?

options.A: Families legally own all medical equipment kept inside the home
options.B: Patients will otherwise refuse to pay their insurance copays
options.C: The nurse enters the patient's personal space as a guest
options.D: Hospital regulations require signed consent before assessment

explanation: Because home health nurses work inside a patient's private home, building a respectful, trusting relationship is vital for successful care cooperation. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T7#GNS324_U1_T7_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a way that food preservation methods work?

options.A: By mutating microbial DNA into beneficial human cells
options.B: By removing moisture needed for bacteria to multiply
options.C: By altering temperatures to halt microbial growth
options.D: By using physical or chemical barriers to stop contamination

explanation: Spot on! Preservation stops microbes through drying, cooling, or chemicals—it definitely doesn't turn germs into human cells! [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h6)

question: You examine a child in a rural clinic and notice dry eyes and Bitot's spots. What deficiency should you suspect?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Iron
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Dry eyes and Bitot's spots are textbook signs of a Vitamin A deficiency. Great clinical catch! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why does tertiary health care require much larger financial investments than primary care?

options.A: It requires expensive advanced technology and specialized equipment
options.B: It employs more administrative staff than clinical nurses
options.C: It only serves patients who pay cash upfront for services
options.D: It focuses exclusively on basic community health talks

explanation: Tertiary care deals with complex conditions requiring high-tech diagnostic and therapeutic machinery, which is very costly to buy and maintain. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h4)

question: Which dangerous practice with used needles should every nurse avoid completely?

options.A: Carrying sharps boxes on a trolley
options.B: Dropping syringes into yellow bins
options.C: Recapping used needles by hand
options.D: Checking fill lines on containers

explanation: Never try to recap a needle with your hands! It's one of the leading causes of accidental needle-stick injuries in nursing. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)

question: What is widely recognized as one of the biggest threats to public health in any population?

options.A: Excessive availability of public park spaces
options.B: Strict enforcement of local sanitation laws
options.C: Widespread poverty and economic instability
options.D: High levels of cultural diversity in neighborhoods

explanation: Poverty makes it super hard for people to afford basic needs like good food, shelter, and healthcare, which naturally drags down health outcomes. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h3)

question: What chemical feature makes a fatty acid 'saturated'?

options.A: It only comes from plant sources
options.B: It stays completely liquid at room temperature
options.C: It has no double bonds between carbon atoms
options.D: It has multiple double bonds in the chain

explanation: Saturated fats are packed tightly together with single bonds only, which is why butter (a saturated fat) stays solid at room temperature! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h2)

question: A nurse administrator checks a mobile medical unit. Which action best shows readiness for action?

options.A: Ordering excess supplies to fill every available inch of storage space
options.B: Relying entirely on local cellular networks for all emergency communication
options.C: Waiting until a disaster is officially declared before checking equipment
options.D: Verifying that supply carts and trauma kits match standardized inventory checklists

explanation: Using checklists ensures that every essential drug and piece of trauma gear is present and fully functional before deployment. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which component of cigarette smoke reduces the oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood?

options.A: Tar
options.B: Nicotine
options.C: Ammonia
options.D: Carbon monoxide

explanation: Carbon monoxide binds tightly to hemoglobin in red blood cells, pushing out oxygen and reducing the amount of oxygen delivered to the heart and other tissues. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T15#GNS213_U1_T15_h5)

question: What does 'pharmacokinetics' actually mean?

options.A: The financial cost of manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs
options.B: The chemical structure of a synthetic compound
options.C: How a medication binds to specific cellular receptors
options.D: What the body does to a drug through absorption and excretion

explanation: Think of pharmacokinetics as the journey of the drug: absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. You can master this! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why do nurses collect a microbiological specimen from a patient?

options.A: To measure the exact white blood cell count in the blood
options.B: To clean out infected tissue from an open wound
options.C: To determine the patient's blood type for transfusion
options.D: To identify the specific microorganism causing an infection

explanation: We collect these samples to find out exactly which germ is making the patient sick, so treatment can hit the right target! [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h1)

question: What is a main nursing duty right when a disaster hits and patients start coming in?

options.A: Funding international relief groups
options.B: Sorting and triaging injured patients
options.C: Rewriting national health emergency policies
options.D: Designing permanent building rules

explanation: During an emergency, checking and sorting patients by how badly they need help is a core nursing job. You've got a bright future in healthcare! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T11#GNS315_U1_T11_h5)

question: Why is it important to write down the exact color and look of the drainage?

options.A: It helps track whether bleeding is resolving or worsening
options.B: It determines the exact antibiotic needed for an infection
options.C: It proves to the insurance company that the nurse was busy
options.D: It shows how much water the patient drank by mouth

explanation: Seeing the color shift from dark red to a clear pink lets you know if the surgical site is finally calming down. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T23#GNS212_U1_T23_h8)

question: Why is it important to formally retire older, outdated protocols when introducing a new one?

options.A: It clears away mental and physical space so new practices can take root
options.B: It ensures that doctors do not have to write any more prescriptions
options.C: It prevents patients from reading old medical textbooks in the library
options.D: It saves money on printing paper for the hospital administration office

explanation: Stopping old, useless habits prevents confusion and reduces the workload burden on busy nurses. [learn more](GST319_U1_T5#GST319_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the main role of ATP in the body?

options.A: Transporting oxygen molecules directly to the brain cells
options.B: Regulating the total volume of blood in circulation
options.C: Serving as the primary energy currency for cellular work
options.D: Acting as a structural support fiber for major organs

explanation: ATP is like the body's cash currency. It carries energy packets directly to where they are needed so your cells can perform their daily tasks. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h2)

question: An older resident taking blood pressure pills suddenly feels dizzy and takes a fall. What should the nurse think of first?

options.A: An immediate need to discharge the resident home.
options.B: The complete absence of any pharmacological influence.
options.C: A normal reaction that requires no clinical follow-up.
options.D: A potential adverse drug reaction or cumulative medication effect.

explanation: Dizziness and sudden falls in older adults are classic clues that a medication might be lowering their blood pressure too much or making them drowsy. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is a main goal of universal health coverage supported by proper funding?

options.A: Building private clinics for wealthy politicians
options.B: Stopping all medical training programs in universities
options.C: Ensuring everyone gets needed health services without financial hardship
options.D: Making all hospital treatments completely free of charge forever

explanation: Universal coverage means health care is accessible to all people without plunging them into debt. [learn more](GST322_U4_T2#GST322_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is one of the most common reasons nurses face malpractice claims in the ward?

options.A: Wearing incorrect uniforms
options.B: Writing incorrect patient notes
options.C: Refusing overtime shifts
options.D: Medication errors

explanation: Giving the wrong drug or incorrect dose is a leading cause of legal trouble. Always double-check your '5 Rights' of medication! [learn more](GST321_U10_T7#GST321_U10_T7_h4)

question: Long-term hookworm infection most commonly leads to which major health problem?

options.A: Chronic kidney failure
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Obstructive jaundice
options.D: Iron-deficiency anemia

explanation: Hookworms hook onto the intestinal wall and feed on blood, which over time causes significant blood loss and leads to iron-deficiency anemia. [learn more](GST114_U3_T6#GST114_U3_T6_h4)

question: A patient has a stroke affecting the left frontal lobe. As a nurse, what sign might you notice?

options.A: Total loss of hearing in both ears
options.B: Complete blindness in the left eye
options.C: Difficulty with voluntary movement on the right side
options.D: Inability to recognize familiar faces

explanation: The frontal lobe handles movement. Because brain pathways cross over, the left side of your brain controls the right side of your body! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T7#GNS211_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is the tiny working unit of the kidney that makes urine?

options.A: Neuron
options.B: Lobule
options.C: Alveolus
options.D: Nephron

explanation: You've got this! The nephron is the main filtering unit of the kidney that cleans the blood and creates urine. Think of millions of these little guys working hard inside each kidney. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T7#GNS121_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why might you prefer the interquartile range over the simple range when looking at how long patients stay in the hospital?

options.A: It is much faster to calculate by hand without a calculator
options.B: It ignores extreme outliers like a few patients staying for months
options.C: It directly measures the exact average of the data set
options.D: It includes every single data point in the final calculation

explanation: Sometimes a couple of patients stay for months and throw off the simple range. The interquartile range focuses on the middle 50% so you get a clearer picture of a normal stay. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T5#GNS217_U4_T5_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a warning sign of worsening breathing trouble that patients should watch out for at home?

options.A: Increasing swelling in the lower limbs
options.B: Improved appetite and steady weight gain
options.C: Inability to speak in full sentences
options.D: Blue discoloration around the lips

explanation: Eating well and gaining steady weight are signs of recovery! The other options show the patient is getting worse and needs help urgently. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T13#GNS123_U3_T13_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of nursing interventions in family-centered care?

options.A: To make all healthcare decisions on behalf of the household head
options.B: To strengthen the family's ability to care for its members independently
options.C: To permanently remove sick family members into institutions
options.D: To eliminate the need for doctors

explanation: Good nursing support empowers families so they gain confidence to manage their health challenges over time. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is avoiding all medications during pregnancy sometimes dangerous?

options.A: Untreated maternal health conditions can reduce oxygen and nutrients to the fetus
options.B: The placenta will release toxins if no drugs are present in the blood
options.C: Fetal organs will stop developing without chemical stimulation
options.D: Maternal hormones require medication to remain stable

explanation: Keeping the mother healthy is the best way to protect the baby. Uncontrolled sickness can starve the baby of vital oxygen and nutrients! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h1)

question: How can you, as a nurse, help a patient build resilience during a long, hard recovery?

options.A: By isolating them from family members to encourage independence
options.B: By doing every single daily task for them to avoid stress
options.C: By helping them focus on controllable factors and celebrating small victories
options.D: By telling them to ignore all negative feelings completely

explanation: Big recoveries are overwhelming. Breaking goals down into small wins helps patients feel capable and gives them the strength to keep going. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h8)

question: What is the main legal risk if a nurse forgets to document a medication right after giving it?

options.A: The hospital computer system will delete the patient file
options.B: The pharmacy will automatically double the next scheduled dose
options.C: The patient's insurance company will refuse to pay the bill
options.D: Legally, the medication is considered unadministered

explanation: In nursing law, if it isn't charted, it didn't happen! Always document promptly to protect your license and your patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T1#GNS122_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why is it crucial to give quick feedback to staff after they submit an incident report?

options.A: It fulfills mandatory legal requirements for hospital tax exemptions
options.B: It stops patients from filing lawsuits against the medical facility
options.C: It shows staff that reporting leads to real system fixes rather than silence
options.D: It ensures that the nurse who made the mistake gets publicly reprimanded

explanation: When staff see their reports fix problems, they trust the system and keep speaking up to keep everyone safe. [learn more](GST319_U6_T5#GST319_U6_T5_h6)

question: A 65-year-old worker with long-term chemical exposure comes in with tiredness. Which background factor makes you suspect a blood issue?

options.A: The geographical location of the local grocery store
options.B: The patient's marital status and living arrangements
options.C: The patient's preferred method of daily transportation
options.D: Occupational chemical exposure linked to bone marrow problems

explanation: Workplace exposure to chemicals like benzene can damage the bone marrow and lead to blood issues over time. Always ask about your patients' jobs! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T2#GNS311_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which of these findings is completely normal and NOT a sign of heart stress?

options.A: A resting heart rate of 120 beats per minute
options.B: A regular resting pulse rate of 75 beats per minute
options.C: A blood pressure reading consistently above 140/90 mmHg
options.D: An apex beat displaced far to the left of the midclavicular line

explanation: A pulse of 75 bpm sits right in the middle of the normal 60–100 range. Nothing to worry about here! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h8)

question: When you suspect a notifiable disease, what patient detail is MOST critical to record?

options.A: Patient's favorite food and dietary preferences
options.B: The brand of soap used in the patient's household
options.C: Patient's correct address and contact information
options.D: The specific color of the patient's bedsheets

explanation: Exactly! Public health officers need a correct address and phone number so they can find the patient and trace contacts fast. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h4)

question: How should a healthcare team view a patient who relapses after months of being sober?

options.A: As a signal to review and adjust the treatment plan rather than a total failure
options.B: As an intentional crime that requires immediate notification of law enforcement
options.C: As an expected physical cure that means treatment is permanently finished
options.D: As definitive proof that the person is hopeless and should be abandoned

explanation: Just like managing hypertension or diabetes, a setback in a chronic condition means we tweak our approach, not give up on the patient! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h6)

question: Why do nurses treat Wernicke encephalopathy as a true emergency?

options.A: It triggers sudden high blood pressure that never responds to drugs
options.B: It can cause quick, permanent brain damage if treatment is delayed
options.C: It quickly spreads as a contagious infection
options.D: It causes immediate paralysis in all four limbs

explanation: You got it! Because it affects the brain so fast, replacing thiamine right away is crucial to prevent lasting harm. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T7#GNS222_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why can't a nurse officially diagnose a patient with diabetes based on just one high random blood sugar test?

options.A: Glucometers cannot measure glucose above 150 mg/dL
options.B: Blood sugar levels never stay high for long periods
options.C: It is a screening test and needs confirmatory tests
options.D: Only laboratory nurses are allowed to make a diagnosis

explanation: Meals, stress, and illness can cause temporary spikes. Doctors rely on fasting tests or HbA1c to make a formal diagnosis. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T19#GNS222_U2_T19_h5)

question: About how long is the duodenum in an adult human?

options.A: Two meters
options.B: Ten centimeters
options.C: One hundred centimeters
options.D: Twenty-five centimeters

explanation: Spot on! The duodenum is the very first part of your small intestine, measuring about twenty-five centimeters (or roughly ten inches) long. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T7#GNS213_U3_T7_h1)

question: Why must a nurse check skin sensation below the level of a spinal cord injury?

options.A: To calculate the daily fluid intake requirements
options.B: To identify areas lacking sensation that are at high risk for unseen injuries
options.C: To check if the patient can still taste and smell normally
options.D: To determine if the patient will ever walk again without assistance

explanation: When patients cannot feel pain or heat, a tiny scratch or hot water can cause severe damage without them even knowing. Regular checks keep them safe! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T17#GNS225_U5_T17_h4)

question: What clinical advantage does seeing a patient at home give a nurse?

options.A: A chance to test all household appliances for electrical safety
options.B: Instant access to advanced surgical laboratories inside the bedroom
options.C: Direct observation of real-life living habits, diet, and daily mobility
options.D: The ability to order X-rays without consulting a medical doctor

explanation: Visiting the home reveals practical challenges like poor pantry stock or tripping hazards that a hospital room hides. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T11#GNS324_U1_T11_h4)

question: What does the frequency column in a distribution table tell a researcher?

options.A: The total number of missing patient files
options.B: The mathematical average of the dataset
options.C: How many times a specific value occurs
options.D: The exact date the data was collected

explanation: Frequency simply counts the number of times a particular score, category, or observation appears in the dataset. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h4)

question: During a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure, what is injected into the uterus to make the tubes visible on an X-ray?

options.A: Sterile normal saline
options.B: Liquid medical silicone
options.C: Radioactive glucose solution
options.D: Radiopaque contrast dye

explanation: Doctors use a special contrast dye so that X-ray machines can clearly trace the fluid as it flows through the womb and down the fallopian tubes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T26#GNS216_U5_T26_h6)

question: Why must mast cell stabilizer sprays or drops be used regularly *before* an allergy season starts?

options.A: They interact with stomach acid if taken after an allergic attack starts.
options.B: They prevent cell rupture proactively but cannot reverse a reaction already underway.
options.C: They build up a thick physical barrier inside the nose that blocks dust.
options.D: They take at least two full weeks to enter the bloodstream for the first time.

explanation: Exactly! Think of them as prevention champs—they stop cells from popping, but they can't clean up the mess if the histamine has already spilled out. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T8#GNS215_U6_T8_h5)

question: What report should a nurse fill out right away after a medication near-miss or error?

options.A: Discharge summary report
options.B: Financial audit report
options.C: Public health census report
options.D: Incident report

explanation: Incident reports let the hospital look at safety issues objectively so they can prevent the same thing from happening again. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h5)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with joint pain and a rash two weeks after receiving horse serum for a snakebite. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: A normal side effect of venom
options.B: An acute anaphylactic shock
options.C: Serum sickness
options.D: A bacterial wound infection

explanation: Spot on! The 1 to 3 week timeline plus exposure to animal-based treatment is a textbook picture of serum sickness. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h3)

question: When should you refer a post-abortion client to a mental health specialist?

options.A: When the client shows signs of severe depression or suicidal thoughts
options.B: Whenever the client has a mild headache
options.C: Every single time a client asks for a prescription for pain medicine
options.D: Only when the client refuses to take iron tablets

explanation: While basic emotional support is part of everyday nursing, deep psychological distress, severe depression, or self-harm threats need expert psychiatric help. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T007#GNS226_U5_T007_h6)

question: Which expense usually takes up the biggest slice of a hospital's budget?

options.A: Patient dietary services
options.B: Office stationery supplies
options.C: Facility security contracts
options.D: Healthcare personnel salaries

explanation: Correct! Paying the dedicated nurses, doctors, and support staff who keep the hospital running takes up the largest share of operating costs. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why is disease surveillance often called an early warning system?

options.A: It predicts exact weather conditions for disease outbreaks.
options.B: It helps health workers spot unusual patterns before an epidemic grows.
options.C: It automatically cures patients before they visit the hospital.
options.D: It replaces the need for laboratory testing entirely.

explanation: Spotting rising cases early lets health workers jump in and take action before a tiny bump turns into a full-blown outbreak! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T93#GNS214_U1_T93_h1)

question: What is the medical term when heart muscle cells suffer from a temporary lack of blood flow and oxygen?

options.A: Hypertrophy
options.B: Regurgitation
options.C: Arrhythmia
options.D: Ischemia

explanation: Ischemia simply means a tissue is crying out because it's starved of proper blood flow. Catching it early in clinical practice saves heart muscle! [learn more](GNS111_U2_T4#GNS111_U2_T4_h6)

question: A patient with a fever is breathing fast and sweating. What kind of fluid loss is happening here?

options.A: Measurable fluid output
options.B: Third-space fluid shift
options.C: Insensible fluid loss
options.D: Gastrointestinal loss

explanation: Exactly! It's called 'insensible' because we can't easily measure it with a jug or a catheter—it just silently evaporates away through breath and skin. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T10#GNS121_U2_T10_h5)

question: What kind of data do we usually analyze using a Chi-Square test?

options.A: Ratio level measurements
options.B: Paired interval scores
options.C: Continuous numerical data
options.D: Categorical data

explanation: You've got this! A Chi-Square test is used for data that falls into distinct groups or categories (like male/female or yes/no), rather than numbers on a continuous scale. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T13#GNS217_U4_T13_h1)

question: What is the main goal of professional communication in nursing?

options.A: To ensure the doctor has less paperwork to do
options.B: To pass the time during long hospital shifts
options.C: To build trust and coordinate safe patient care
options.D: To prevent patients from asking too many questions

explanation: Spot on! As nurses, everything we say is designed to put the patient at ease and keep their care safe and organized. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T2#GNS112_U3_T2_h1)

question: Why should community nurses use simple everyday language and live demonstrations during health talks?

options.A: To discourage people from asking questions during lectures
options.B: To ensure clear understanding and encourage practical application by listeners
options.C: To make the teaching session take as little time as possible
options.D: To hide complex medical terminology from uneducated citizens

explanation: Exactly! Keeping it simple ensures everyone follows along and can actually practice what they learned when they go home. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h6)

question: What is the quick check a nurse does every time they put on an N95 to check the seal called?

options.A: Qualitative sweet test
options.B: Sterile pressure scan
options.C: Manufacturer inspection
options.D: User seal check

explanation: It is a quick self-check you do every single time you put on your respirator to make sure it is sitting right. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h5)

question: In a community health project, money, medical supplies, and trained personnel are known as what?

options.A: Inputs
options.B: Outcomes
options.C: Outputs
options.D: Impacts

explanation: Inputs are the raw resources, funds, and staff you put *in* to get the project started. You've got this! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T21#GNS225_U2_T21_h2)

question: What should a nurse do if a visitor enters an isolation room without wearing the required PPE?

options.A: Ignore it if they promise not to touch the patient
options.B: Ask another staff member to handle the situation later
options.C: Report the visitor to hospital security immediately
options.D: Politely stop them, explain the rules, and help them put on PPE

explanation: Educating visitors and ensuring they wear correct gear prevents breaches in the barrier system. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: When is a nurse most likely to initiate intravenous therapy for a patient?

options.A: When the patient needs a rapid correction of severe dehydration.
options.B: When the patient is eating normally and taking daily multivitamin pills.
options.C: When topical skin cream is prescribed for a localized rash.
options.D: When a mild headache needs to be relieved over an eight-hour period.

explanation: Severe dehydration requires quick fluid volume restoration directly into the blood vessels, which can only be achieved effectively through IV therapy. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h1)

question: Which part of the brain is the main bridge between the nervous and endocrine systems?

options.A: Hypothalamus
options.B: Thalamus
options.C: Medulla oblongata
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: That's correct! The hypothalamus acts as the chief coordinator, linking brain signals to hormone control. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T1#GNS211_U1_T1_h2)

question: You are filling out a referral form for a pregnant mum with severe pre-eclampsia. What is the most important clinical finding to write down?

options.A: Her personal opinion about hospital food quality
options.B: The distance from her house to the primary healthcare center
options.C: The name of her local community youth organization
options.D: Her most recent blood pressure reading and urine protein test

explanation: Brilliant! Vital signs like her BP and protein levels give the incoming delivery and doctor team immediate, life-saving information. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h3)

question: What kind of flavor experience does the umami taste sensation give us?

options.A: The biological indicator for sugars
options.B: The baseline detection of sodium
options.C: The savory taste of amino acids
options.D: The sharp warning signal of acids

explanation: Umami gives food that rich, savory goodness! It is triggered by amino acids like glutamate, helping your body detect and enjoy protein-packed meals. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T10#GNS211_U4_T10_h1)

question: A patient at home is alert and refuses a scheduled dressing change. What is your best first move as a nurse?

options.A: Perform the procedure anyway since the doctor ordered it
options.B: Abandon the patient immediately and end your home care contract
options.C: Explain the risks of refusing, write down the details, and notify the doctor
options.D: Ask family members to force the patient to accept the treatment

explanation: Well done! Patients have a right to refuse care. Your job is to make sure they understand the risks, document everything clearly, and keep the medical team updated. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T5#GNS324_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary protein lost in the urine during nephrotic conditions?

options.A: Globulin
options.B: Fibrinogen
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Hemoglobin

explanation: Albumin is the most abundant protein in the blood and the main one that leaks through the damaged glomerular barrier into the urine. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h1)

question: As a community health nurse, what is your very first step when starting a referral?

options.A: Calling an ambulance service before assessing the patient
options.B: Asking the patient to pay administrative referral fees
options.C: Writing a discharge summary for the local health board
options.D: Identifying a clinical condition that exceeds the clinic's capacity

explanation: You've got this. The referral process only begins once you realize the patient's medical needs are too advanced for your local clinic to handle alone. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h4)

question: A patient with a chest stab wound suddenly loses their pulse and shows PEA (pulseless electrical activity) on the monitor. What is the best immediate action?

options.A: Wait for a formal chest X-ray to confirm the cardiac arrest
options.B: Place the patient in a flat, prone position to rest the back
options.C: Administer oral blood pressure medications through a feeding tube
options.D: Prepare equipment for emergency thoracotomy and active resuscitation

explanation: Traumatic arrest with PEA is a critical emergency. It often needs immediate teamwork, resuscitation, and sometimes opening the chest in the trauma bay to save the patient's life. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why is having a blood transfusion service so important in a CEmOC facility?

options.A: To reduce the incidence of newborn jaundice following difficult deliveries
options.B: To prevent mild gestational anemia during routine antenatal clinic visits
options.C: To speed up cervical dilation during the active phase of normal labour
options.D: To replace severe blood loss from conditions like postpartum hemorrhage or placenta previa

explanation: When a mother loses too much blood, quick access to safe blood can literally mean the difference between life and death. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h3)

question: Which secondary source uses math and statistics to combine the results of many different studies?

options.A: Primary clinical trial
options.B: Narrative textbook chapter
options.C: Meta-analysis
options.D: Case study

explanation: Awesome! A meta-analysis pools numbers from several studies together to give us a powerful big-picture answer. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T6#GNS217_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which part of the brain connects the nervous system to the endocrine system?

options.A: Cerebral cortex
options.B: Medulla oblongata
options.C: Hypothalamus
options.D: Cerebellum

explanation: The hypothalamus is the master bridge! It takes messages from the brain and turns them into hormonal orders. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T4#GNS211_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the key difference between formative and summative assessment?

options.A: Formative assessment guides ongoing learning, while summative assessment certifies final competence
options.B: Formative assessment is always graded, while summative assessment is optional
options.C: Formative assessment occurs at the end of a course, while summative assessment occurs at the start
options.D: Formative assessment tests physical skills, while summative assessment tests memory

explanation: Formative check-ins help you learn along the way, while summative tests (like finals) check if you've mastered the whole topic. [learn more](GST321_U8_T2#GST321_U8_T2_h7)

question: Why is careless handling of needles and blades such a big deal in the hospital?

options.A: It damages expensive hospital instruments quickly
options.B: It causes patients to lose trust in the nursing staff
options.C: It can transmit dangerous infections to anyone nearby
options.D: It leads to immediate disciplinary action by management

explanation: A used sharp can easily pass germs straight into the bloodstream through a break in the skin. Always handle with care! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h1)

question: What is a common myth people believe about using digital tools in nursing practice?

options.A: People believe computers can completely replace all doctors and nurses.
options.B: People think digital materials can only be used by illiterate community members.
options.C: People assume mobile phones do not require any battery power to operate.
options.D: People believe digital tools completely replace traditional face-to-face nursing contact.

explanation: Digital tools are awesome helpers, but they can never replace the warmth and trust of real human touch and face-to-face nursing care. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to monitor organ function regularly in patients with systemic autoimmune conditions?

options.A: It prevents patients from developing contagious bacterial infections
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future blood tests
options.C: Widespread inflammation can silently damage vital organs like the kidneys and heart
options.D: It proves whether the patient is following their prescribed diet

explanation: Systemic flare-ups don't just hurt joints—they can quietly cause internal damage over time, making routine checkups a lifesaver. [learn more](GST114_U4_T8#GST114_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which tool is used to hold the surgical needle securely when repairing an episiotomy?

options.A: Needle holder
options.B: Mucus extractor
options.C: Anatomical fetoscope
options.D: Cord scissors

explanation: A needle holder gives you a firm, non-slip grip so you can pass your stitches smoothly and comfortably. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T10#GNS225_U3_T10_h5)

question: Why do clinical instructors use structured grading tools instead of just going with their personal feelings?

options.A: To ensure students never fail a clinical placement.
options.B: To eliminate the need for written examinations entirely.
options.C: To reduce the total amount of time spent grading students.
options.D: To reduce personal bias and ensure fair, objective grading.

explanation: Structured tools keep grading fair and consistent for everyone, so your grade depends on your skills, not the instructor's mood. Keep up the great studying! [learn more](GST321_U9_T3#GST321_U9_T3_h1)

question: Why do we need to manage hospital waste carefully?

options.A: To maintain a pleasant smell throughout the hospital wards
options.B: To reduce the overall cost of hospital administrative duties
options.C: To ensure that all medical supplies are completely recycled
options.D: To prevent infections, toxic injuries, and sharp punctures

explanation: Hazardous waste carries germs and dangerous materials that can easily hurt patients, hospital staff, and the public if we aren't careful. [learn more](GST114_U6_T8#GST114_U6_T8_h1)

question: What is a major safety concern when giving sleeping pills (sedative-hypnotics) to older adults?

options.A: Severe respiratory alkalosis
options.B: Hypertensive crisis
options.C: Permanent hearing loss
options.D: Increased risk of falls

explanation: Sleeping pills can cause daytime drowsiness and dizziness, making older adults unsteady on their feet and putting them at a high risk for accidental falls. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T12#GNS123_U3_T12_h7)

question: Why does handing out certificates fail if a manager ignores broken equipment and chronic understaffing?

options.A: Because hygiene factors like basic working conditions must be addressed first
options.B: Because nurses only care about financial bonuses and nothing else
options.C: Because certificates decrease the intrinsic drive of veteran nurses
options.D: Because recognition programs are illegal in most healthcare settings

explanation: Paper awards can't fix a stressful environment with broken gear and too few hands. Basic working conditions must be sorted out first! [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h4)

question: Which of these is an example of using an endoscope for treatment (therapeutic)?

options.A: Measuring the patient's resting blood pressure
options.B: Taking a routine chest X-ray of the lungs
options.C: Drawing blood for a complete blood count
options.D: Removing a polyp from the colon lining

explanation: Great job! When we use a scope to actively fix something—like snipping out a polyp—it's therapeutic. If we're just looking around, it's diagnostic. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h2)

question: If expired drugs leak from an illegal dumpsite into a community well, what is the main danger?

options.A: Residents drinking the water will ingest harmful pharmaceutical substances
options.B: Local children will contract instant needle-stick injuries from the water
options.C: The borehole pump will rust and break down due to paper waste clogging
options.D: Mosquito breeding sites will multiply rapidly inside the deep water pipes

explanation: You nailed it. Chemicals and drugs seeping into underground water directly poison the drinking water supply for the community. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h3)

question: What physical sign strongly suggests a wound is developing a local bacterial infection?

options.A: Clear, watery fluid leaking in small amounts
options.B: Purulent drainage and surrounding redness
options.C: Rapid tightening of the surrounding scar tissue
options.D: Cool skin temperature around the dressing edges

explanation: Pus and redness are classic signs that white blood cells are fighting a heavy bacterial invasion in the tissue. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is a team approach involving different professions so important when helping trafficking survivors?

options.A: Doctors are legally barred from talking to police officers
options.B: No single profession has all the skills needed for complex recovery
options.C: Legal frameworks prevent nurses from providing basic medical care
options.D: Psychological counseling is the only treatment survivors require

explanation: Trafficked children have diverse medical, emotional, and legal needs that require different experts working together seamlessly. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T25#GNS225_U5_T25_h7)

question: Why is understanding the family life cycle important for a community health nurse?

options.A: It determines exact genetic disorders in newborns
options.B: It helps predict the specific stressors and health needs a family faces at each age
options.C: It proves if the family is registered with local government
options.D: It allows you to calculate household income

explanation: Every life stage has its own unique health risks, helping you know what guidance or preventive care to offer next. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T3#GNS124_U2_T3_h3)

question: A maternity team wants to reduce postpartum bleeding. Which option is the best, most practical aim statement?

options.A: Reduce postpartum hemorrhage rates by 30% across the maternity ward over the next four months
options.B: Ensure that all midwives are properly trained in modern obstetric emergency response techniques
options.C: Stop postpartum bleeding completely by purchasing more uterotonic drugs for the clinic
options.D: Make sure every patient giving birth receives high-quality and compassionate nursing care

explanation: A great goal is specific, easy to measure, and has a clear timeline. This option hits all three marks! [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h2)

question: Which factor is most critical for a nurse to verify before initiating provider-assisted partner notification?

options.A: The local government tax clearance certificate of the couple
options.B: Whether the partner owns a smartphone or a television set
options.C: The informed consent and safety status of the index client
options.D: The exact bank balance and employment status of the partner

explanation: Patient safety comes first; partner notification must never endanger the index client or proceed without their explicit agreement. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h6)

question: A patient asks how to view their recent laboratory test results from home. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Guide the patient on how to access their secure online health portal
options.B: Print the entire hospital database and mail it to their home
options.C: Tell the patient that viewing lab results is strictly illegal for laypeople
options.D: Read all hospital lab results out loud over a public phone call

explanation: Nurses empower patients by showing them how to use secure patient portals to check their own health records. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: What exactly is a pure culture?

options.A: An agar plate covered in twenty different types of bacteria
options.B: A liquid broth that has been filtered to remove all water
options.C: A culture containing only a single species of microorganism
options.D: A water sample taken from a deep underground well

explanation: Great job! A pure culture holds just one type of organism, making it easy to study its unique traits without distractions. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main goal of preparing a modified-texture diet for a patient with swallowing difficulties (dysphagia)?

options.A: To eliminate all sodium and fats from daily caloric intake
options.B: To reduce the visual appeal of food so the patient eats less
options.C: To increase the speed of carbohydrate digestion in the stomach
options.D: To prevent the risk of choking and aspiration during swallowing

explanation: Changing food consistency makes swallowing safe, protecting the patient's airway from food or liquid going down the wrong pipe. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T008#GNS227_U3_T008_h6)

question: How does an emotionally intelligent nurse leader handle a dispute between two staff members?

options.A: By publicly reprimanding both nurses during the morning handover meeting
options.B: By immediately issuing formal query letters without discussing the root cause
options.C: By ignoring the dispute and hoping the nurses resolve it on their own
options.D: By listening to both sides calmly and guiding them toward a constructive resolution

explanation: Great choice! An emotionally intelligent leader uses patience and communication to solve conflicts and keep the team spirit high. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h6)

question: A patient with a tracheostomy suddenly struggles to breathe, turns bluish, and you can't pass a suction catheter down the tube. What is likely happening?

options.A: Normal post-operative recovery
options.B: A mucous plug blocking the airway
options.C: The cuff is completely deflated
options.D: The oxygen flow rate is too high

explanation: If your catheter won't go through and the patient is in distress, a thick mucous plug is usually blocking the pipe. This is an urgent call for action! [learn more](GNS315_U4_T1#GNS315_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is a major clinical indication for the immediate emergency referral of a pregnant woman?

options.A: Severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia
options.B: Mild morning sickness during the first trimester
options.C: Physiological ankle swelling after long standing
options.D: Normal vertex presentation at 36 weeks

explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia poses an immediate, life-threatening risk of seizures and stroke, requiring urgent transfer to a facility capable of managing complications. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h6)

question: Which of these clinical signs tells you a child has SEVERE dehydration?

options.A: Lethargy or floppiness and sluggish skin pinch
options.B: Restless behavior and dry oral mucosa
options.C: Eager and rapid drinking from a cup
options.D: Normal tear production when crying

explanation: When a child is very sleepy, floppy, or their skin pinch takes a long time to go back, that's a red flag for severe fluid loss requiring urgent medical help. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h5)

question: How does placing an advanced breathing tube (like an endotracheal tube) change how CPR is performed?

options.A: Rescuers can give continuous compressions without pausing for breaths
options.B: Medications can only be given directly through the breathing tube
options.C: Chest compressions are stopped entirely while artificial breaths are given
options.D: Defibrillation pads are no longer needed once the tube is inserted

explanation: Once the tube is secured, teamwork gets easier—compressors can keep pushing without stopping to give breaths every few seconds! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h7)

question: What is the main goal of studying food, milk, and water microbiology?

options.A: Measuring the exact vitamin content in fresh farm produce
options.B: Creating new chemical preservatives for processed meals
options.C: Finding ways to completely sterilize all natural water bodies
options.D: Studying microbes that spoil consumables or cause illness

explanation: Great job! This area of microbiology focuses on finding and understanding the tiny germs that contaminate what we eat and drink, so we can prevent sickness. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which animal is well-known as the natural reservoir host for transmitting Lassa fever in West Africa?

options.A: Mastomys rat
options.B: Anopheles mosquito
options.C: Domestic livestock
options.D: Migratory birds

explanation: The multimammate rat (Mastomys) carries the Lassa virus and sheds it in homes through its urine and droppings. Good public health detail to keep in mind! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h4)

question: Which group of patients is included in home care for cognitive impairments?

options.A: Healthy adults with no medical history
options.B: Patients with conditions like dementia and Alzheimer's disease
options.C: Athletes recovering from a broken ankle
options.D: Children with acute seasonal allergies

explanation: Dementia and Alzheimer's disease cause cognitive decline requiring specialized safety and management strategies at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h7)

question: What usually happens when nurse managers are left out of hospital financial planning?

options.A: Nursing salaries will increase without administrative review
options.B: Units may suffer from underfunding and increased staff burnout
options.C: Patients will experience faster recovery times on the wards
options.D: Hospitals will automatically receive higher government grants

explanation: If nursing leaders don't have a seat at the financial table, budgets get made without realizing how short-staffed and overworked the wards will be. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h8)

question: Why is it important to discuss proper medication storage during counselling?

options.A: Heat and moisture can break down drug potency
options.B: Expired pills turn into nutritional supplements
options.C: Refrigeration doubles the active dose strength
options.D: Plastic bottles attract dangerous insects

explanation: Improper storage in humid or hot places like bathrooms can ruin the chemical stability of medications. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do right after a shock is delivered?

options.A: Resume chest compressions right away
options.B: Administer a routine dose of IV atropine
options.C: Draw blood samples for arterial blood gas analysis
options.D: Check the carotid pulse for up to one minute

explanation: Don't pause to check for a pulse immediately! Modern resuscitation rules tell us to jump right back into chest compressions to keep blood flowing. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T17#GNS213_U1_T17_h5)

question: A patient with active TB needs to go for an X-ray in another part of the hospital. What must the nurse do?

options.A: Ensure the patient wears an N95 respirator mask
options.B: Have the patient wear a standard surgical mask
options.C: Transport the patient during peak visiting hours
options.D: Instruct the patient to hold their breath in hallways

explanation: You've got this! Putting a simple surgical mask on the patient catches their respiratory droplets right at the source while they are moving through the hospital. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T96#GNS214_U1_T96_h5)

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their birth control method?

options.A: Forgetting clinic locations
options.B: Traveling out of the country
options.C: Experiencing side effects
options.D: Changing religious beliefs

explanation: When clients face physical or emotional side effects that they don't know how to handle, they usually stop using the method. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h4)

question: Your patient is prescribed sucralfate along with other oral medications. How should you time their doses?

options.A: Give sucralfate immediately after meals alongside all other pills
options.B: Mix all drugs into the same liquid suspension for convenience
options.C: Crush all medications together and administer them simultaneously
options.D: Separate sucralfate and other oral drugs by at least two hours

explanation: Because sucralfate forms a sticky coating, it can trap other drugs and stop your body from absorbing them. Give other meds a 2-hour window! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T1#GNS223_U3_T1_h5)

question: Which household practice comes from a misunderstanding about how HIV is spread?

options.A: Refusing to share eating utensils with the patient
options.B: Using separate towels for drying after a bath
options.C: Sleeping in the same room with proper ventilation
options.D: Washing the patient's clothes with regular soap

explanation: You're doing great! HIV is not spread through saliva or by sharing spoons, forks, and cups during meals. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T6#GNS216_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the main focus of Behavioral Change Communication (BCC) in nutrition?

options.A: Addressing cultural habits and beliefs influencing food choices
options.B: Importing expensive nutritional supplements from abroad
options.C: Enforcing strict legal penalties for poor dietary habits
options.D: Conducting laboratory tests on food chemical safety

explanation: That's right! BCC looks past simple facts to understand the cultural and social reasons behind how people choose and prepare their meals. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T17#GNS214_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the main goal of the health team concept in patient care?

options.A: To deliver the highest quality of care through shared work
options.B: To ensure doctors make all final decisions independently
options.C: To lower the overall financial cost of running a clinic
options.D: To reduce the number of hospital staff on duty daily

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare is a team sport. By working together, different professionals combine their skills to give patients the absolute best care possible. [learn more](GST321_U7_T2#GST321_U7_T2_h1)

question: A ward successfully tested a new handoff communication checklist with one nurse for a week. What is the most logical next step?

options.A: Immediately fire all staff who refuse to use the old checklist
options.B: Expand the test to include all nurses on that specific shift for another week
options.C: Abandon the checklist because testing is now complete
options.D: Mandate the checklist for every hospital in the entire country immediately

explanation: You nailed it! Scaling up should happen step-by-step—moving from one person to a small group before trying a wider rollout. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is a major social barrier that stops young people from visiting a health clinic?

options.A: Lack of electricity in the clinic waiting room
options.B: Excessive availability of free medication
options.C: Too many books in the facility library
options.D: Fear of being judged or stigmatized by healthcare workers

explanation: Nobody wants to be lectured or looked down on. When health workers show moralizing attitudes, young people stay far away from the clinic. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h5)

question: What is the main goal of quality improvement (QI) in nursing?

options.A: Cutting down nursing staff to reduce hospital costs
options.B: Punishing staff who make medication mistakes
options.C: Filing incident reports after safety errors happen
options.D: Proactively redesigning care to give patients better outcomes

explanation: Great job thinking ahead! Quality improvement is all about fixing systems before errors happen, rather than just reacting after things go wrong. You've got this! [learn more](GST319_U1_T4#GST319_U1_T4_h1)

question: In clinical nursing, how do we truly know how much pain a patient is in?

options.A: Pain only exists if visible tissue damage is present.
options.B: Pain is whatever the experiencing patient says it is.
options.C: Pain is a psychological illusion created by anxiety.
options.D: Pain can be accurately measured solely by high blood pressure.

explanation: Remember this golden rule of nursing: pain is subjective. If the patient says it hurts, it hurts! Always trust and validate your patient's report. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T1#GNS321_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the term for a patient's right to make independent decisions about their own medical treatment?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Negligence
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Malpractice

explanation: Correct! Autonomy simply means self-rule—giving every competent patient the full right to make their own healthcare choices. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T5#GNS324_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the best initial nursing action if a patient has a painful ingrown toenail that looks a bit red?

options.A: Soak the foot in warm water and report it to the provider
options.B: Dig out the ingrown corner immediately using sterile forceps
options.C: Cut a deep V into the center of the nail to relieve pressure

question: What is the main goal of the fluid released by the bulbourethral glands?

options.C: To provide primary nutrition for sperm
options.D: To neutralize acid in the urethra

question: What event signals the secondary oocyte to finish its final cell division (meiosis II)?

options.A: A sharp rise in vaginal pH

options.C: The process of implantation
options.D: The entry of a sperm cell

question: Why is it wonderful for Nigerian nurses to recommend local soups like ugwu and egusi during nutrition talks?

options.A: They are affordable, culturally familiar, and rich in essential nutrients
options.B: They are the only foods allowed by traditional customs during pregnancy
options.C: They replace the need for antenatal clinic attendance
options.D: They completely eliminate the risk of gestational high blood pressure

explanation: Our local soups are packed with vitamins, iron, and good fats! They are easy to find, pocket-friendly, and nourishing. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h6)

question: How do effective unit managers keep patients safe during tough staff and resource shortages?

options.A: By charging patients exorbitant fees for basic cotton wool
options.B: By pretending that the shortages do not exist at all
options.C: By turning away every single patient who walks through the door
options.D: By using creative resourcefulness and strong advocacy skills

explanation: Brilliant! Even when resources are tight, resourceful managers find safe workarounds and fight hard for what their ward needs. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h8)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what BMI value marks the start of the overweight category?
explanation: The overweight category officially starts at a BMI of 25.0 and goes up to 29.9. You are learning fast! [learn more](GNS227_U1_T015#GNS227_U1_T015_h3)

question: What is your immediate priority if the clinic vaccine refrigerator breaks down completely?

options.A: Transfer vaccines to a backup cold box or facility
options.B: Open all vaccine vials to let the trapped heat escape
options.C: Wait patiently for the repair technician to arrive
options.D: Discard all stored vaccines into regular waste bins

explanation: Act fast! Moving the vaccines to a backup cool box or nearby facility saves them from spoiling while you call for repairs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T65#GNS214_U1_T65_h7)

question: What was the main characteristic of the health care model before the Alma-Ata conference?

options.A: It relied entirely on traditional herbal practitioners in rural areas
options.B: It focused primarily on community-based disease prevention
options.C: It was heavily curative and concentrated in urban hospitals
options.D: It provided free universal insurance for all citizens equally

explanation: Before Alma-Ata, global health systems focused on treating sick patients in city-based hospitals rather than preventing disease in communities. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T2#GNS124_U1_T2_h2)

question: In the diathesis-stress model, what does 'diathesis' refer to?

options.A: An underlying vulnerability or predisposition
options.B: The chemical name for antipsychotic drugs
options.C: A sudden environmental crisis or life event
options.D: A physical test used to measure brainwaves

explanation: Diathesis represents the biological or psychological vulnerability a person carries before a major stressor triggers an illness. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the ultimate goal of patient education when teaching someone how to care for their diabetes at home?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever experiencing normal life stress
options.B: Eliminating all future visits to the primary healthcare clinic
options.C: Empowering the patient to safely manage their daily condition
options.D: Ensuring the family takes complete control of medication administration

explanation: Good education gives patients the tools, knowledge, and confidence to take charge of their own health every day. Love to see it! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h8)

question: Why should nurses avoid heavy medical jargon when talking to community members?

options.A: Using simple words makes the nurse appear less educated to patients
options.B: Jargon automatically cures diseases faster than simple language
options.C: Patients may become confused and fail to understand the required health action
options.D: Medical terms are illegal to use outside of a hospital laboratory setting

explanation: Keep it simple! Using everyday language ensures everyone—regardless of their reading level—understands how to protect their health. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T7#GNS124_U5_T7_h4)

question: Why should parents praise a gifted child's hard work rather than their raw smarts?

options.A: To prevent the development of crippling perfectionism
options.B: To speed up asynchronous physical growth rates
options.C: To eliminate the need for specialized schooling
options.D: To guarantee university admission later in life

explanation: Praising effort teaches kids that it's okay to make mistakes and try again. Praising 'smartness' can make them terrified of failing later on. Beautiful learning moment! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T1#GNS225_U5_T1_h5)

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of an underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism)?

options.A: A fast and pounding heartbeat
options.B: Shaking hands and muscle tremors
options.C: Intolerance to cold temperatures
options.D: Sudden and unexplained weight loss

explanation: You nailed it! When the metabolism slows down due to low thyroid hormone, patients feel chilly even when everyone else is warm. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T2#GNS222_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a normal heart finding in a healthy pregnant woman?

options.A: Soft systolic heart murmur
options.B: Persistent crushing chest pain
options.C: Mild resting tachycardia
options.D: Mild dependent ankle edema

explanation: Spot on! Chest pain is never normal in pregnancy and always needs quick medical investigation. You are doing fantastic! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T2#GNS121_U7_T2_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a current challenge facing community health nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Funding shortages for public health programs
options.B: Infrastructural deficits in rural clinics
options.C: The double burden of infectious and non-communicable diseases
options.D: Zero prevalence of any health problems in the country

explanation: You got it! Nigeria definitely still deals with various health challenges, so saying there are zero problems isn't true. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h7)

question: Which medication is commonly given during cardiac arrest to boost blood flow to the heart and brain?

options.A: Epinephrine
options.B: Atropine
options.C: Digoxin
options.D: Warfarin

explanation: You'll see epinephrine used often in codes! It acts as a powerful vasoconstrictor to push blood where it's needed most during resuscitation. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h7)

question: Which topical preparation is oil-based, greasy, and best suited for thick, dry, scaly skin lesions?

options.A: Aqueous solution
options.B: Gel
options.C: Ointment
options.D: Lotion

explanation: Ointments have a high oil content which creates a protective seal over the skin, locking in moisture and treating dry skin conditions effectively. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h3)

question: What is the main job of a 'cold chain' logistics system when moving food around?

options.A: Perishable items from spoiling by maintaining low temperatures
options.B: Dry grains from getting wet during heavy rain
options.C: Livestock from escaping transport trucks
options.D: Metal cans from rusting inside storage warehouses

explanation: A cold chain keeps a continuous refrigerator system going from the farm all the way to the store shelf so perishables stay fresh. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h6)

question: When should a puncture-resistant safety box for used syringes be sealed and prepared for disposal?

options.A: When it is filled up to the three-quarters mark
options.B: At the end of every working hour regardless of volume
options.C: When every single inch to the absolute brim is packed
options.D: Only when an external supervisor visits the clinic

explanation: Stopping at three-quarters prevents overfilling and lowers the risk of accidental punctures from protruding needles. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h7)

question: What are the classic red flags of a thyrotoxic storm?

options.A: Dangerous high fever and rapid heart rate
options.B: Sudden numbness in the lower legs
options.C: Low body temperature and slow breathing
options.D: Severe dehydration with zero ketones

explanation: Think of a thyrotoxic storm as the body's engine revving completely out of control—leading to high fever, severe tremors, and a racing heart (tachycardia). [learn more](GNS222_U2_T16#GNS222_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why must you teach patients never to stop their blood pressure medication suddenly?

options.A: It leads to sudden severe hair loss within hours.
options.B: It permanently damages the liver enzymes.
options.C: It can trigger dangerous rebound hypertension.
options.D: It will cause an immediate permanent loss of taste.

explanation: Spot on! Stopping blood pressure meds abruptly can cause blood pressure to shoot right back up to dangerous levels. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T2#GNS313_U3_T2_h5)

question: On which side of the patient should a nurse stand when assisting them to walk with a gait belt?

options.A: At least two meters ahead of them
options.B: On the patient's weaker side
options.C: Directly behind the patient's back
options.D: On the patient's stronger side

explanation: Standing on the weaker side allows the nurse to provide the necessary physical support if the patient begins to lean or buckle. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h3)

question: Why do the testes hang outside the main body cavity in the scrotum?

options.A: To shorten the length of the vas deferens tube
options.B: To allow easier passage of urine through the urethra
options.C: To protect the internal organs from high abdominal pressure
options.D: To keep sperm production at a slightly lower temperature

explanation: Brilliant! Sperm cells need a temperature slightly cooler than normal body heat to develop properly. The hanging scrotum acts like a natural cooling system. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T8#GNS311_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which clinical sign is a classic indicator of respiratory distress in a newborn?

options.A: Strong, rhythmic sucking reflexes
options.B: Regular, deep, quiet breathing
options.C: A pink, warm skin appearance
options.D: Intercostal chest retractions

question: How do most families in Nigeria pay for home health care services?

options.A: Through corporate employer-sponsored packages
options.B: Through direct out-of-pocket spending by families
options.C: Through free government welfare grants
options.D: Through comprehensive national health insurance schemes

explanation: You nailed it. Since health insurance usually doesn't cover home care, families pay straight from their own pockets. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which group in the community is usually hit hardest by nutritional food taboos?

options.A: Young adult working males
options.B: Pregnant and lactating women
options.C: Unmarried teenage boys
options.D: Elderly male community leaders

explanation: Expectant and breastfeeding mothers need extra nutrition, which unfortunately makes them prime targets for restrictive cultural rules. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h4)

question: Which hospital expense usually goes up as more patients are admitted?

options.A: Annual administrative software licenses
options.B: Facility property insurance premiums
options.C: Monthly building mortgage payments
options.D: Disposable syringes and IV tubing

explanation: Medical supplies are variable costs. More patients mean you use more supplies, so the total price goes up. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h5)

question: A patient with gallbladder trouble feels pain up near their right shoulder blade. What is this called?

options.A: Referred pain
options.B: Phantom pain
options.C: Rebound tenderness
options.D: Somatic pain

explanation: Referred pain happens when internal organs and skin areas share the same spinal cord pathways, tricking the brain into feeling the pain somewhere else. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: What often happens when patients simply cannot afford the high cost of their prescribed medications?

options.A: Pharmacies are forced to give all drugs away
options.B: They may skip doses or stop taking them
options.C: Hospital admissions instantly drop to zero
options.D: They automatically receive free government refills

explanation: Exactly. When out-of-pocket costs are too high, patients often try to stretch their drugs by skipping doses, which delays their healing. [learn more](GST322_U5_T1#GST322_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which clinical sign points more toward a clotting factor problem like haemophilia rather than a platelet issue?

options.B: Frequent, mild nosebleeds that stop within minutes
options.C: Tiny red spots on the skin after minor pressure
options.D: Bleeding into large joints like the knees and elbows

explanation: Bleeding into big joints (called hemarthrosis) is a classic trademark of factor deficiencies like haemophilia. Petechiae and nosebleeds are usually more about platelet trouble. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h5)

question: Why must nurse leaders assess the current environment before trying to change the culture?

options.A: To comply with building safety codes and fire regulations
options.B: To find out which individual staff members need immediate firing
options.C: To gather baseline data and identify specific problem areas
options.D: To calculate the exact budget required for annual staff bonuses

explanation: You're right! Assessment helps leaders see what's really happening so they can target actual problems rather than just guessing. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h3)

question: What is a major advantage of tele-counselling in modern dietary practice?

options.A: Completely replacing the need for any human communication
options.B: Breaking down distance barriers to make regular follow-ups easier
options.C: Guaranteeing that every patient has perfect internet connection
options.D: Requiring all patients to have expensive medical equipment at home

explanation: Tele-counselling allows patients in remote or distant areas to speak with healthcare providers without travelling. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T002#GNS227_U7_T002_h7)

question: When should a nurse teach a client to apply cold packs rather than heat to an arthritic joint?

options.C: Only when the weather turns very cold outside

question: A nurse draws up the wrong dose of insulin, but catches the mistake before giving it to the patient. What is this called?

options.A: A systemic failure
options.B: An adverse event
options.C: A sentinel event
options.D: A near miss

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to getting contraceptives in Nigeria?

options.B: Stockouts of essential commodities at health facilities
options.C: Judgmental attitudes from healthcare workers
options.D: Universal availability of free home-delivery services

question: Which common childhood condition should a psychiatric nurse screen for alongside a behaviour disorder?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia
options.B: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
options.C: Type 1 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Chronic kidney disease

question: When a nurse checks a mother's perineal area during a postnatal visit, what are they mainly looking for?

question: What is reported as the most common barrier to HIV disclosure?

options.A: Forgetting one's own diagnosis date

options.C: Excessive availability of antiretroviral drugs
options.D: Fear of stigma and discrimination

question: Why do patients recovering from severe heart trauma need continuous heart rhythm monitoring?

options.A: Rhythm strips are legally required to prove the surgery was successful.

options.C: Damaged heart tissue can trigger dangerous irregular heart rhythms days after the injury.
options.D: The electrical system of the heart heals instantly and never causes issues later.
