question: Why should you as a nurse always ask your patients if they use traditional herbs or local remedies?

options.A: To report illegal practitioners to the local authorities
options.B: To calculate the exact economic cost of local healthcare
options.C: To prevent dangerous interactions with hospital medications
options.D: To replace all expensive hospital drugs with free herbs

explanation: Patients often mix local herbs with hospital drugs without mentioning it. Checking for this helps keep them safe from unexpected drug reactions. You're learning to think like a safe, caring nurse! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T2#GNS125_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is it important to speak up and report physical discomfort early on?

options.A: It guarantees an immediate promotion to head nurse
options.B: It allows management to reduce the staff member's salary
options.C: It prevents minor aches from turning into disabling injuries
options.D: It is required before a nurse can take a lunch break

explanation: Exactly! Catching little aches and pains early means you can fix them before they turn into major health problems. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T3#GNS113_U3_T3_h8)

question: What is the primary purpose of giving a patient a diuretic?

options.A: To increase urine output and remove excess body fluid
options.B: To dissolve hard kidney stones blocking the ureter
options.C: To raise the blood pressure during episodes of fainting
options.D: To stop painful muscle cramps in the lower extremities

explanation: Diuretics make the kidneys flush out extra water and salt, which is wonderful for reducing swelling and fluid overload in conditions like heart failure. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h7)

question: Why must nurse-led dietary education consider a patient's cultural background and financial situation?

options.A: Hospital policies legally require patients to eat traditional hospital meals

options.C: Dietary advice only works if the patient can afford the foods and actually enjoys eating them
options.D: Financial status determines how fast human cells absorb dietary fiber

explanation: Patients are much more likely to stick to a meal plan if it respects their cultural food preferences and fits comfortably within their budget. Great job thinking practically! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h7)

question: Which of the following is an example of objective, professional nursing documentation?

options.C: Client cried during family visits and verbalized feeling hopeless.
options.D: Client is acting crazy and refusing to talk to anyone today.

explanation: Professional documentation records observable behaviors and direct client statements without personal judgment or bias. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h8)

question: What happens inside the eye if the fluid drainage gets blocked while the eye keeps making more fluid?

options.D: Eye pressure goes up

question: Why would a healthcare planner choose a Cost-Utility Analysis over a regular Cost-Effectiveness Analysis?

options.A: To calculate only the direct financial profits of a new pharmacy wing
options.B: To evaluate treatments that impact both length of life and patient well-being
options.C: To prove that all medical interventions cost the exact same amount
options.D: To avoid measuring clinical outcomes entirely in hospital settings

explanation: When patient comfort and quality of life matter just as much as living longer, a Cost-Utility Analysis (using QALYs) is the best choice. [learn more](GST322_U2_T5#GST322_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why might a standard keyword search miss relevant articles that a MeSH search would easily find?

options.C: Standard keywords are illegal to use in evidence-based practice
options.D: Computers cannot read lowercase letters in standard search bars

question: Why would a patient with a severe head injury and a dropping Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score be put on a ventilator?

options.A: Airway protection
options.B: Chronic lung disease
options.C: Metabolic alkalosis
options.D: Primary heart failure

question: Why do multiple humanitarian agencies need to work together during a major refugee crisis?

options.A: International agencies prefer to work in complete isolation from locals.
options.B: Government health ministries are legally banned from helping refugees.
options.C: It eliminates the need for any professional nursing staff on site.
options.D: No single organization has all the resources required to meet complex needs.

explanation: Crises are massive! Providing shelter, clean water, food, and healthcare all at once requires teamwork and pooled resources from many different organizations. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T21#GNS225_U5_T21_h7)

question: What is the primary reason nurses perform frequent neurovascular checks on a casted limb?

options.C: To measure how fast the bone is knitting back together
options.D: To determine the exact weight of the plaster cast material

question: A nursing student writes this objective: 'To study everything about nurses.' Which SMART rule does this break the most?

options.C: Time-bound
options.D: Ethical

question: Which of these is a vital disease-prevention shot routinely given during pregnancy clinics in Nigeria?

options.C: Chemotherapy infusion
options.D: Joint replacement surgery

question: Why does a teenage boy's voice crack and deepen?

options.C: Elongation of the vocal cords due to laryngeal cartilage growth
options.D: Swelling of the tonsils caused by an upper respiratory infection

question: Which symptom is a classic sign of a vulvovaginal yeast infection (candidiasis)?

options.A: Yellow-green, frothy discharge with strawberry spots
options.B: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with intense itching
options.C: Thin, gray-white discharge with a strong fishy odor
options.D: Clear, watery discharge with severe lower abdominal pain

question: How would a patient most likely contract iatrogenic Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease?

options.A: Through a contaminated surgical tool

options.C: By inheriting a mutated genetic trait
options.D: By eating undercooked beef products

question: At what age does the posterior fontanelle usually close up?

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour food recall to check what a patient eats?

options.B: Patients may forget or misreport what they actually ate
options.C: It only measures physical height rather than food
options.D: It takes over a week to complete a single interview

question: How is rehabilitation different from acute care?

options.A: Managing sudden spikes in vital signs
options.B: Providing emergency life-saving surgical interventions
options.C: Curing the underlying acute infectious disease
options.D: Achieving maximum independence and quality of life

explanation: Acute care fixes the sudden emergency, but rehab is all about helping your patient get back on their feet and live life to the fullest over the long haul. You've got this! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T2#GNS314_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why must patients on warfarin keep their daily intake of green leafy vegetables steady?

options.A: High fiber diets speed up kidney excretion of the drug
options.B: Vitamins in plants cause rapid breakdown of red blood cells
options.C: Vegetables contain vitamin K which directly counteracts warfarin
options.D: Leafy greens bind to the stomach wall and block absorption

question: In a hospital pharmacy, what does the FEFO inventory rule stand for?

options.D: Fastest Earnings From Outpatients

question: Which of these is a main dietary goal for preventing lifestyle diseases?

options.A: Eliminating all forms of protein from meals
options.B: Reducing excessive salt and sugar intake
options.C: Doubling daily caloric consumption
options.D: Eating only imported canned foods

explanation: Spot on! Cutting down on too much salt and sugar is a powerful way to help prevent conditions like hypertension, obesity, and diabetes. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T14#GNS313_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why is daily movement so important for patients who are stuck on bed rest?

options.A: It cures underlying chronic medical conditions completely
options.B: It prevents the loss of muscle strength and joint flexibility
options.C: It guarantees a shorter hospital stay for every patient
options.D: It eliminates the need for pain medication administration

explanation: Lying in bed all day makes the body weak very quickly. Simple daily movements stop muscles from wasting away and keep joints moving smoothly. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T4#GNS221_U1_T4_h1)

question: What makes blunt force trauma to the abdomen so dangerous?

options.A: Permanent stiffening of the peripheral joints
options.B: Immediate infection of the superficial skin layers
options.C: Rapid development of severe seasonal allergies
options.D: Massive internal bleeding without visible external wounds

explanation: A person can look fine on the outside while bleeding heavily inside. That's why careful, hands-on nursing assessment is always key! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is a great example of modern digital tech used in nursing education today?

options.A: Virtual reality software for viewing detailed human anatomy
options.B: Passing paper textbook chapters around a crowded classroom
options.C: Using a chalkboard to draw basic diagrams of bone fractures
options.D: Writing physical notes with ink on animal skin parchment

explanation: VR and digital apps take learning to a whole new level by bringing 3D depth to complex topics like human anatomy. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h5)

question: Why are low-molecular-weight heparins so convenient for patients compared to standard heparin?

options.A: They last for an entire month with just one injection
options.B: They never cause any bleeding or immune reactions
options.C: They can be mixed directly into drinking water for easy mornings
options.D: They use standard weight-based doses without needing routine aPTT blood tests

explanation: That's the beauty of LMWH! Because the dose is predictable based on the patient's weight, patients can take them easily without constant pinpricks for aPTT tests. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T5#GNS223_U1_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following is considered a direct source of data for maternal mortality?

options.A: General household census questionnaires
options.B: Retrospective community interviews about sisters
options.C: Hospital admission and delivery registers
options.D: Mathematical models based on neighboring countries

explanation: Hospital registers and civil registration records capture actual events directly as they are documented in health facilities or official registries. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h3)

question: How is the outside of the home visiting bag treated during a visit?

options.A: As a clean working surface
options.B: As sterile and clean
options.C: As contaminated
options.D: As safe for food storage

explanation: The outside of the bag touches various surfaces during travel and home entry, so it is always treated as contaminated. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T11#GNS225_U2_T11_h3)

question: How can we best describe a 'system' in a busy healthcare setting?

options.A: Interdependent parts working together to achieve a common goal
options.B: A single computer program used to record daily patient vitals
options.C: An isolated department that operates entirely on its own
options.D: The strict disciplinary rules enforced by the hospital director

explanation: Think of a hospital like a football team: every department connects with and relies on the others to make sure the patient gets better safely. [learn more](GST319_U2_T7#GST319_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which standard lab test checks a patient's hemoglobin and hematocrit levels directly?

options.A: Complete blood count
options.B: Coagulation screen
options.C: Basic metabolic profile
options.D: Liver function panel

explanation: The good old Full Blood Count (or Complete Blood Count) is your go-to test for looking at red cells, hemoglobin, and all things blood-related in the ward! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h4)

question: At what age might a nurse suspect a motor issue if an infant consistently prefers using only one hand?

options.A: By one month of age
options.B: Only during school age
options.C: Before eighteen months
options.D: Around three years old

explanation: Babies usually don't show a strong hand preference early on. Showing one-sided preference before 18 months can be an early sign of hemiplegic cerebral palsy. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h4)

question: A nurse is checking the chart before giving IV ondansetron. Which pre-existing heart condition means you need to be extra careful?

options.A: History of peptic ulcers
options.B: Prolonged QT interval
options.C: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.D: Mild essential hypertension

explanation: Spot on! 5-HT3 drugs can affect heart electrical rhythms, so a patient with a long QT interval is at risk for serious heart rhythm issues. Safety first in nursing! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T6#GNS223_U3_T6_h3)

question: What happens to the pupils of your eyes when the parasympathetic system is stimulated?

options.A: No change in pupil size
options.B: Uncontrolled twitching
options.C: Pupil dilation
options.D: Pupil constriction

explanation: Parasympathetic signals make the circular muscles in your iris contract, which causes your pupils to constrict (get smaller). Keep going, you've got this! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T31#GNS211_U3_T31_h5)
